scenes.name: The Booth

say: Harborline Financial. We watch the money move.
Say something. He's doing the statue thing.

beats.caption: A labor bureau card: median pay $129,180 (May 2025), across all experience levels, not starting pay.
It lists 21 percent growth, from 2025 to 2035.

say: Why this seat, and not a free shirt?
I want to get good at this. Fast.
Then stay. The shift will test that.

options.rem: Marcus will remember you wanted to get good.

say: I need the job. I'll show up.
Good. Showing up is the rare part.

options.rem: Marcus will remember you promised to show up.

say: That pay number is hard to ignore.
Honest. Keep that habit when it gets loud.

options.rem: Marcus will remember you were honest about the money.

say: The pause ends it. Think faster next time.

options.rem: Marcus will remember the pause.

say: Nights teach you what the rules are for.
Nights, policy, or the startup across the aisle.
Put me on the night shift.
Direct. I can work with direct.

options.rem: Marcus will remember you asked for nights.

say: I want rules, audits, the policy side.
Then watch the mess first. Nights, then rules.

options.rem: Marcus will remember you asked for policy.

say: I want to hear the startup's pitch.
Big voice, tiny room. Have fun.

then.caption: You pocket the startup's card. Then you walk back.

options.rem: Jordan will remember you almost walked.

say: I'll slot you for nights. Decide to like it later.

options.rem: Marcus will remember you froze at the booth.

say: Don't lose the badge before you start.
I'll keep dinner sad and warm for you.

beats.caption: The badge is yours. Work starts after dark.

scenes.shot_notes: Marcus waits behind the Harborline booth as the crowd bumps past. Jordan watches you, enjoying this too much.

scenes.name: Cram Night

say: I made you flashcards. Be nice about it.
Security Plus, the ISC2 starter, or sleep.
You're on tonight. Try to look alive.
Employed and scared. My favorite kind.

options.rem: Jordan will remember you crammed Security+.

say: The ISC2 starter. Walk me in.
Small bites. I respect the plan.

options.rem: Jordan will remember you started with ISC2 CC.

say: Future you can be mad. Go to work.

options.rem: Jordan will remember you closed the laptop.

say: Blink once if the cards won.

options.rem: Jordan will remember the stare.

say: One card. Weird address, and it will not stop.

options.rem: Jordan will remember you said to cut it off.
Jordan will remember you wanted the logs.

say: At this hour they're a rumor.

options.rem: Jordan will remember you wanted a grownup.

say: Time's up. You stop the bleeding first.

options.rem: Jordan will remember you blanked on a flashcard.

say: If you froze, we call that a result.
Pocket it. The real room is darker.

beats.caption: The shift starts. The room is cold and bright.

scenes.shot_notes: Jordan fans flashcards on the kitchen counter. The new badge sits beside a cold mug.

scenes.name: Monday

say: You cut it off, then wrote the story. That's the job.
You read first. It kept talking while you read.
You asked who else to wake. You already had me.
You went quiet. I pulled the plug. Thin writeup.
Monday is for ego checks. Welcome in.
Sit. I read the ticket. Now talk me through it.
One breath. What did you trust out there?
A strange address. So I moved.
Good. Be able to say it again.

options.rem: Marcus will remember you owned the call.

say: I'm not sure I called it right.

options.rem: Marcus will remember you asked to be corrected.

options.t: The tools should have caught it.

say: The tools should have been louder.
They scream all day. You pick one.

options.rem: Marcus will remember you blamed the tools.

say: Words. I don't grade silence twice.

options.rem: Marcus will remember the long pause.

say: Every alert gets a story. Keep writing yours.
Coffee here is bad. That part will not change.
Go home, rookie. Sleep while you can.

scenes.shot_notes: Marcus sets a paper cup down and stays standing. The night ticket glows on your monitor.

scenes.name: The Door

say: You look chewed up. Is the bank standing?
You've been a ghost since the badge.
Work was weird. I can't share details.

options.rem: Jordan will remember you kept the details at work.

say: A finance laptop called a strange address.
I will forget that on purpose.

options.rem: Jordan will remember you overshared.

say: Ask me after I've actually slept.
Copy. The couch is neutral ground.

options.rem: Jordan will remember you chose the couch.
Jordan will remember you stood in the doorway.

say: Text me if the building eats you.
Shoes off. You made it back. That counts.

beats.caption: The badge stays by the door. The queue does too.

scenes.shot_notes: You drop the badge in a bowl by the door. Jordan looks up from the couch, already grinning.

scenes.name: On Loan

say: You survived Monday. Did Marcus yell?
You've got ticket face. It's a whole look.
It went fine. That's all I can say.

options.rem: Jordan will remember you kept work at work.

say: I didn't know the rule, so I asked.
Asking is underrated. Says me, who never asks.

options.rem: Jordan will remember you admitted asking.

say: I want to read the actual policy. All of it.
On purpose? For fun? Okay, nerd.

options.rem: Jordan will remember you wanted the policy.

say: Cool. Talk to the bowl. It's a great listener.

options.rem: Jordan will remember you stared at the bowl.

beats.caption: Your phone buzzes. A message from Dana Whitfield, Security Director.
"Marcus showed me your ticket. You wrote down why, not just what."
"That's judgment about process. Risk and compliance needs it. You're on loan to them next week."

say: Loaned out? Like a library book?
Day shift, though. I get my roommate back.

beats.caption: The badge stays by the door. Next week it opens a different room.

scenes.shot_notes: You drop the badge in the bowl by the door. Jordan looks up from the couch, fork stuck in a takeout box.

scenes.name: Pizza Pitch

say: Don't be mad. I brought pizza and my boss.
Theo Grant. Kestrel Pay. I've heard a lot.
We do payments for the small shops big banks ignore.
We move real money. Right now nobody guards the door.
That's where you come in. Act surprised.
First security hire. The whole program, built your way.
The bank has a ladder. I have an elevator.
Jordan says you're certified. Customers love a certificate.
What's broken right now? Be honest.
Everything, a little. That's the fun part.

options.rem: Theo will remember that.

say: Who do I report to, and who can overrule me?
Me. And nobody, mostly. We'll figure it out.

options.rem: Theo will remember that.

say: An elevator sounds great. When do I start?

options.rem: Jordan will remember that.

say: The quiet ones always say yes. Take a slice.

options.rem: Theo will remember that.

say: Monday. Bring a laptop. Ours are mostly stickers.
Roommates and coworkers. What could go wrong?

beats.caption: Two weeks later, the bank badge goes back in an envelope.

scenes.shot_notes: Jordan shoulders the door open with two pizza boxes. Theo Grant follows in a sharp jacket, looking around like he might buy the place.

end: The first night is logged. The queue will still be there tomorrow.

ends.text: You traded a ladder for an elevator. Nobody mentioned who maintains it.
One night on the floor. Next stop, the room that writes the rules.
The first night is logged. The queue will still be there tomorrow.
